AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVE
AbstractText.content: This study investigated whether the inflammation-based Glasgow prognostic score (GPS) predicted the prognosis of patients with endometrial cancer (EC) in terms of progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS).

AbstractText.Label: STUDY DESIGN
AbstractText.content: Pretreatment GPS was examined to determine the correlations with recurrence and survival in 431 patients with EC. Statistical analyses were performed using the Mann-Whitney U test. PFS and OS were analyzed using the Kaplan-Meier method. Cox's proportional hazard regression was used for univariate and multivariate analyses.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: Median PFS and OS were 49.7 and 52.7 months, respectively. The follow-up range was 1 to 140 months. Kaplan-Meier analysis revealed that patients with EC cancer and high GPS (GPS 2) had a shorter PFS and OS than those with lower GPS (GPS 0+1) (PFS: P<0.001; OS; P<0.001). On multivariate analysis, GPS (GPS 2) was an independent predictor of both recurrence (P<0.001) and survival (P<0.001) for all cases of EC.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: GPS can be useful as an indicator of poor prognosis in patients with EC.
